title: Used Suno and Cursor to finally update my free 6-year-old solo game!
author: Delicious_Yam_4177
selftext:
I probably will get a lot of hate for this, but I did it! I've become a huge advocate for AI tools recently, especially after using them to revive a project close to my heart.

Six years ago, I completely built a game called **Rocket Bots** all by myself. It had some old, pesky bugs and was missing the right soundtrack. Since I already proved to myself back then that I could do it all from scratch, I felt I earned the right to use some modern assistance to finally polish it.

I used Cursor to help me efficiently hunt down and squash those old code bugs, and I fed Suno my own original music compositions to generate the perfect soundtrack for the game. When you feed AI your own data, it's definitely not stealing, it's just scaling your own creativity.

Beyond that, AI is a massive, game-changing **help for disabled people** who might otherwise face physical or cognitive barriers when coding or composing. It opens doors that used to be closed.

The improvement to my game is massive! I tried sharing this milestone with the general Godot community, but it was unfortunately rejected due to their strict anti-AI stance. I wanted to share it here instead with people who appreciate how these tools can help solo devs and creators expand their work.   
  
**AI lets go**!
